source_scope.paper: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents, arXiv:2605.07594v2
source_scope.model_artifact_main_commit: 32c9274 (Hugging Face short revision shown by public UI, committed 2026-05-29)

findings.claim: MemCompiler provides a science-domain matched delivery intervention with the same retrieved task memory candidate pool: on Qwen-2.5-14B ScienceWorld, full state-conditioned compilation scores 46.67 completion / 69.33 partial versus AMMI static injection of the same retrieved M at 27.93 / 52.68. The paper explicitly says this AMMI row injects the same retrieved M and isolates dynamic compilation. This is stronger evidence than a generic retrieval-vs-no-retrieval comparison, but it still changes the whole delivery/compilation mechanism rather than only a final accept/reject bit for an already-selected item.
findings.scope_guard: Do not interpret as exact per-step selected-memory-identity-fixed acceptance-only ablation. Candidate pool M is matched; per-step compiled m* is deliberately different under SCMC and absent as a selector under AMMI.

findings.claim: The current official ScienceWorld runner retrieves Task Memory once per episode from task_text before the execution loop, then passes the same task_memory object together with current observation, score, working memory and history to the Manager at every step. Thus current public code implements fixed episode-level candidate-pool retrieval plus per-step state-conditioned Manager guidance, not per-step bank retrieval.
findings.scope_guard: Claim is about current public revision ec5a579...; it is not an exact binding to the paper's evaluated revision.

findings.claim: The current public ScienceWorld detailed trajectory records Manager inputs/outputs and only a task_memory_summary count, not stable IDs/digests for the exact candidate-pool members or a machine-readable identity for the per-step memory entry selected/compiled into guidance. Therefore an offline replay cannot establish exact per-item fixed-retrieval causality from the logged trace alone without additional instrumentation.
findings.scope_guard: This is an observability/provenance limitation of the inspected public runner, not evidence that the authors did not use richer private logs.

findings.claim: The official project page now links a 44.8 GB Hugging Face model artifact whose public history has two commits on 2026-05-29. This partially resolves the prior search for an external evaluated artifact, but the model has no model card and the inspected public surfaces do not bind it to a particular Table-3 run, memory-bank snapshot, or candidate-pool digest.
findings.scope_guard: Public learned-model artifact found; immutable evaluated memory snapshot and exact run binding remain unresolved.

primary_public_evidence: arXiv HTML v2: fixed task-memory candidate pool M is retrieved once at episode start; Memory Compiler compiles m*(t) from current state and M; NOACTION is allowed when no entry is applicable; Table 3 Full=46.67/69.33 ScienceWorld, AMMI static injection same memory=27.93/52.68.

Official GitHub current code: Memcompiler.retrieve_memory(query_task) operates on task-level query; ScienceWorld runner calls it once before while-not-done and reuses task_memory across steps; detailed_out stores task_memory_summary counts rather than exact memory identities.
Official project page links Hugging Face model; public model page shows 44.8 GB and commit 32c9274 on May 29 with no model card.
causal_boundary: Strong same-candidate-pool science-domain evidence for dynamic state-conditioned delivery versus static injection; still not the sought exact fixed selected-item identity + receiver accept/reject-only manipulation.
